venue.name: Port McNeill & District Museum
venue.description: The Port McNeill & District Museum was built with community support to display logging memorabilia from the North Island, and it opened in 2000. Its video exhibits are "The Last Logging Railway in North America", "Women in Log Scaling" and "Finding the Pioneer". The museum's page sits on the Town of Port McNeill website, which marks it open by appointment and says admission is by donation. No school or group programme, price, age range or opening hours are published.

programs.name: Museum visit by appointment
programs.description: The museum displays logging memorabilia from the North Island and shows three video exhibits, on the last logging railway in North America, on women in log scaling, and on finding the pioneer. The page carries no opening hours and is marked open by appointment, so a visit has to be arranged first, by phone. Admission is by donation and greatly appreciated, which is not the same as free, and no child, school or group rate is published. Nothing on the site describes a program built for a class or a daycare group, and it does not say whether a visit is guided or on your own.
programs.what_children_do: Look at displays of logging memorabilia from the North Island and watch the museum's video exhibits about the last logging railway in North America, women in log scaling, and finding the pioneer.
programs.our_note: Phone first. There are no posted opening hours, so the visit has to be arranged, and that call is your only chance to ask the things the site never covers. Worth asking how long a visit runs, whether there is a washroom, and what a group of children is expected to give at the door.
programs.practical_summary: The only practical things published are a phone number and that admission is by donation. Washrooms, lunch space, parking, step-free access, how long a visit takes and what ages the museum suits are all unstated, so plan to ask all of it on the call you make to book.
programs.evidence: Admission is by donation and greatly appreciated
